title: Private minimum pack: Prometheus alerts for latency SLO burn + availability (severity aligned to paging policy)
creator: Aisha Bello
description:
## Goal
Ship a baseline set of Prometheus alert rules for **Redwood Private** installs that cover:
1) **Latency SLO burn** (multi-window burn-rate alerting)
2) **Availability / success-rate** (golden signal)

Rules must be:
- Safe for customer clusters (bounded cardinality)
- Actionable (runbook links + clear annotations)
- Aligned with Private paging policy (page-worthy vs ticket-only)
- Packaged in the Private minimum observability bundle (`observability-pack`) and wired into Helm defaults.

## Context / References
- SLO guidance: `sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/private-install-slo-guidance.json`
- Standards: `sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/metrics-and-alerting-standards-for-private.json`
- Alert severity mapping thread: `sources/slack/eng-sre/1746297701-alert-severity-mapping-private.json`
- Oncall feedback (runbooks in alerts): `sources/slack/eng-oncall/1747334700-runbook-links-needed-in-alert-descriptions.json`

## Proposed alerting philosophy (Private minimum pack)
### Severity / routing
- **severity=page (Sev2 / high)**: customer-facing impact likely; requires human attention within 15–30m.
- **severity=ticket (Sev3 / medium)**: investigate during business hours; non-urgent degradation or early warning.
- **severity=info**: disabled by default; used for diagnosis only.

> Note: We do not ship Sev0/Sev1 paging rules as part of the minimum pack; those remain customer-specific and/or Premium. “page” here maps to Private oncall paging during supported hours per contract.

### Key design choices
- Use **burn rate** alerting for SLO-based conditions (fast + slow windows).
- Avoid per-route / per-tenant labels in alert series by default.
- Prefer **recording rules** from ENG-19144 (req rate, err rate, latency) and alert on those aggregates.
- Separate “symptom” alerts (latency/availability burn) from “cause” alerts (GPU pressure, OOM, etc. in ENG-19148).

## Signals & metric assumptions
This ticket assumes metrics are standardized per ENG-19143/PR-18503 and recording rules exist per ENG-19144.

### Required recorded series (names to match ENG-19144)
- `redwood:request_total:rate5m{component="gateway|runtime"}`
- `redwood:error_total:rate5m{component="gateway|runtime"}` (5xx + transport failures; exclude 4xx by default)
- `redwood:availability_ratio:rate5m{component="gateway|runtime"}` (1 - error_rate)
- `redwood:latency_p95_seconds:5m{component="gateway|runtime"}` OR histogram-based SLO measurement series

For true SLO burn-rate, we need an **SLO indicator** series (ratio of “good events”):
- Availability SLI: good = non-5xx requests (optionally exclude 429 depending on policy)
- Latency SLI: good = requests under latency threshold

If ENG-19144 does not produce “good/total” for latency yet, implement directly in these alert rules using histogram buckets.

## Alert rules (v1)
### 1) Availability SLO burn (multi-window)
Assume a monthly SLO target per component (defaults):
- Gateway availability SLO: **99.9%**
- Runtime (inference request) availability SLO: **99.5%**

Burn-rate alert structure (Google SRE style):
- **Fast burn**: 5m window & 1h window
- **Slow burn**: 30m window & 6h window

#### Alert: `RedwoodPrivateAvailabilitySLOBurnHigh`
- severity: `page`
- Condition: burn rate > 14.4x (would exhaust monthly budget in ~2 days)
- Expression (illustrative; exact depends on final SLO recording rules):
  - `(
      (1 - avg_over_time(redwood:availability_ratio:rate5m{component="gateway"}[5m])) / (1 - 0.999)
    ) > 14.4
    and
    (
      (1 - avg_over_time(redwood:availability_ratio:rate5m{component="gateway"}[1h])) / (1 - 0.999)
    ) > 14.4`
- Annotations must include:
  - `summary`: "Availability SLO burn (fast) for {{ $labels.component }}"
  - `runbook_url`: Confluence runbook section (placeholder until runbook merged)
  - `impact`: "Customer requests failing (5xx/transport)"
  - `triage`: first 3 checks (see below)

#### Alert: `RedwoodPrivateAvailabilitySLOBurnLow`
- severity: `ticket`
- Condition: burn rate > 6x on 30m and 6h windows
- Same annotations requirements

Triage steps (annotation text, concise):
1) Check `redwood:request_total:rate5m` vs baseline (traffic drop vs errors spike)
2) Check rollout/restarts for gateway/runtime (CrashLoopBackoff, OOMKilled)
3) Check upstream dependencies (policy service, model registry integration, auth) if gateway failures


### 2) Latency SLO burn (multi-window)
Default latency thresholds (tunable via Helm values):
- Gateway p95: **1.0s**
- Runtime p95: **2.5s** (inference path; excludes client-side streaming time)

Latency SLI definition (histogram-based):
- good events: requests with duration <= threshold
- total events: all requests (excluding health checks)

Example (needs final metric names):
- `good = sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{le="1.0",component="gateway"}[5m]))`
- `total = sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_count{component="gateway"}[5m]))`
- `latency_sli = good / total`

Then burn uses `(1 - latency_sli) / (1 - latency_slo_target)`.

#### Alert: `RedwoodPrivateLatencySLOBurnHigh`
- severity: `page`
- Windows: 5m and 1h
- burn threshold: 14.4x
- Include `threshold_seconds` in annotations.

#### Alert: `RedwoodPrivateLatencySLOBurnLow`
- severity: `ticket`
- Windows: 30m and 6h
- burn threshold: 6x

Triage steps to embed:
1) Check saturation panels (GPU util, queue depth, batch size) (link to runtime dashboard panels)
2) Check p95 vs p99 divergence (tail latency often indicates queueing)
3) Check error rate increase (latency + errors often capacity)


### 3) Hard availability symptoms (non-SLO) (v1 minimal)
These are “stop-the-world” symptom alerts used when SLO burn math is unavailable due to metric gaps.

#### Alert: `RedwoodPrivateRequestErrorRateHigh`
- severity: `page`
- Condition: 5xx/transport error ratio > 5% for 10m AND request rate > minimal floor
- Guardrail: do not alert when traffic is near-zero (reduce noise after hours)

#### Alert: `RedwoodPrivateRequestRateDropUnexpected`
- severity: `ticket`
- Condition: request rate drops >70% vs 1h baseline (optional; disabled by default due to workload variance)


## Cardinality / label policy for alerts
- Allowed labels on alert series: `cluster`, `namespace`, `component`, `deployment_mode` (vpc|onprem), `region` (if present), `install_id` (if low-cardinality)
- **Not allowed by default**: `tenant_id`, `request_id`, `route`, `model`, `pod` (except for purely infra-level alerts handled elsewhere)
- Any per-model/route alerting is explicitly out-of-scope for minimum pack (Premium / customer-specific).

## Packaging requirements
- Rules go into `observability-pack` under `private/minimum/alerts/latency_availability.yaml`.
- Must include:
  - `labels`: `pack="private-minimum"`, `component=...`, `severity=...`
  - `annotations`: `summary`, `description`, `runbook_url`, `dashboard_url` (Grafana link template), `triage`
- Wire enablement + thresholds into Helm values (via ENG-19152), including:
  - `sloTargets.gatewayAvailability`, `sloTargets.runtimeAvailability`
  - `latencyThresholds.gatewayP95Seconds`, `latencyThresholds.runtimeP95Seconds`
  - `minTrafficRpsToAlert`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Alert rules merged in `observability-pack` with sane defaults and guardrails
- [ ] Severities validated against the paging policy (SRE sign-off)
- [ ] At least one fast-burn and one slow-burn alert per component (gateway + runtime)
- [ ] All alerts include runbook URLs (even if initially internal Confluence links)
- [ ] Smoke test harness (ENG-19156 / PR-18544) can trigger at least one availability and one latency alert in CI
- [ ] No alert rules produce > O(10) series per private install by default

## Open questions
1) Do we count **429** as availability failure for Private SLO? (current leaning: **exclude 429** from availability SLI, but provide separate saturation alerts in ENG-19148)
2) Should gateway and runtime share the same SLO target defaults, or separate as above?
3) Do we have a stable way to compute latency SLI for streaming requests (server processing time vs full stream duration)?

## Implementation notes
- Prefer using `*_bucket` histogram SLI for latency rather than quantiles for burn-rate correctness.
- Add `for:` durations conservatively (e.g., 2–5m fast burn, 10m for error rate) to avoid flapping.
- Coordinate final metric names with Nadia Rahman / Omar El-Sayed if instrumentation differs between gateway and runtime.
comments: 2025-07-10 — Sergio Costa: Drafted alert list + first-pass PromQL using histogram SLI. Waiting on ENG-19144 recording rule names so we don’t bake unstable metric names into alerts.

2025-07-11 — Rafael Mendes (SRE): Please ensure every paging alert includes (a) runbook_url and (b) a dashboard_url pointing to the Private minimum pack dashboards. Also add a traffic floor so low-traffic clusters don’t page on a single blip.
2025-07-14 — Aisha Bello: Confirmed burn-rate thresholds: 14.4x for page (fast burn), 6x for ticket (slow burn). Aligns with our hosted playbook; acceptable for Private with conservative defaults.

2025-07-16 — Nadia Rahman: Gateway histograms are stable; runtime duration histogram label set is being reduced (model/route removed) as part of ENG-19143. Alerts should aggregate without model labels.
2025-07-18 — Tomáš Novák: Add explicit triage text in annotations (“what to do first”), not only links. Oncall feedback is that links alone aren’t enough at 3am.

2025-07-22 — Sergio Costa: Implemented availability burn alerts against `redwood:availability_ratio:*` series; still need final decision on 429 handling. Suggest exclude 429 from availability SLI and add separate ‘rate limited’ ticket alert in a follow-up.
2025-07-23 — Rafael Mendes (SRE): OK with excluding 429 from availability SLI for v1, but document clearly. Also ensure latency SLI uses server-side duration (not full stream).
